decisions.reason: Encrypted second-channel communication remains central to the firm's identity and secure messaging strategy, even if it may now be marketed as part of a broader platform.
Mobile PDF signing still fits the firm's push into app-based interactions and digital contract processes, though it could be bundled into wider signature offerings.
A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is a foundational capability for this firm's cryptography-led business and is likely to stay even if no longer promoted standalone.
The secure email-to-app delivery robot is a narrower tool that is more plausibly absorbed into broader communication products or discontinued after not being visible separately for two years.
The QR-code-based hardware signature token is the least aligned with the firm's software- and app-centric direction and its lack of recent visibility makes withdrawal likely.
Payment security compliance remains relevant for regulated enterprise customers, so the firm would likely retain the capability, albeit possibly as part of a broader security suite.
